'THE RECORDS BEHIND THIS (21 COUNTED, 2 LEFT OUT)' and 'TRUE OF EVERY READ, NOT OF TODAY (2)' are collapsed summaries that state the size of what is behind them before you open them, so you reach a receipt from a claim without leaving the claim. The chrome is also stable across all four modes and the briefing, so a mode switch moves nothing but the content.
candidates.weakest: desk__inbox__owner_signature__390x844__fold.png — at 390 the four row actions become wrapped 14px inline text links on roughly 20px line spacing, with two of the four struck through. 44×44 is not credible here, and at Inbox scale (42 events) the struck-through density will read as noise rather than as discipline.
concerns: Inline text actions at 390 cannot plausibly meet the 44×44 primary-control floor; the Inbox row needs a mobile treatment that is a transformation, not a reflow.

The 'IN THIS READ' section index with its per-section counts and bolded current section is desktop-only. It disappears entirely at 390, which is exactly where the 2383px page most needs a position aid and a way back to the top of a section.
new_user drops the 'THE OTHER MODES' line from the header. The one screen where a reader most needs to know the other three modes are also empty is the only screen whose chrome does not say so.
The header is four stacked bands (products / scope / modes / other-modes) before any content — about 120px, the heaviest chrome of the four at 1440.
Whether the 'IN THIS READ' index is genuinely sticky cannot be confirmed from a still; the bolded active item implies scroll-spy but the behaviour is unverified.

candidates.label: D
strengths: Per-mode state sits under the mode label itself, in words: READ · PARTLY READ · NOT ENOUGH HISTORY · NOTHING IN IT · DID NOT ANSWER · NOTHING SET UP YET. On provider_failure all four flip to a red DID NOT ANSWER and the scope row's verdict flips with a red underline. The difference between a quiet day and a broken provider is in the navigation, not in a banner you can scroll past, and it survives the 2×2 reflow at 390.

The Inbox row is the best-designed interaction in the lab. Live actions are indigo links (Mark as read · Snooze · Clear from Inbox), refused ones are struck grey with the reason inline. Live and refused differ by colour, weight and strike, not by a subtle opacity. Alongside it, 'WHEN A SNOOZE COMES BACK' pre-discloses each snooze option with its exact resolved local time before you commit — journey 6 answered as persistent context instead of a post-hoc toast. Nobody else does this.

The failure band — hairline rules struck through, red rules above and below the sentence — reads as a tear in the page. It is a signature moment that carries meaning rather than spectacle, and it degrades to the same thing at 390. 'THE EDGE OF THIS READ · Nothing below this line is asking for you inside this read' gives the quiet day a subject instead of furniture.
candidates.weakest: rail__my-work__owner_signature__1440x960__fold.png — the rows are inert. No Mark as done, no change-of-owner, and the titles carry no underline or colour, so nothing on the screen reads as openable. Journeys 10 and 11 have no visible surface in the arrival state, on the one mode that is supposed to be a responsibility ledger you act on.
concerns: The mode switcher moves between modes. On today, inbox and my-work the mode row sits at roughly y=223; on rail__analytics__owner_signature__1440x960__fold.png a standfirst is inserted above it and it drops to about y=266. The one element that must not move when you switch modes moves 43px, so every Today↔Analytics switch is a visible jump.
My work rows carry no actions and no link affordance at all.

'See the records behind this' is a bare indigo link with no chevron or plus, so it signals navigating away where Editorial, Index and Desk all signal expand-in-place. On a lens about not losing your place, that is the wrong signal.
The current mode's verdict is stated twice on the same screen — under the mode label and again at the right of the scope row — which at 390 pushes content below the fold for no gain.

The snooze options resolve to 01:30 on 25 October and 02:00 on 28 March. Those are DST-boundary times and the exactness is probably deliberate, but presented unannotated they read as noise rather than as precision.
candidates.requiredCorrection: Anchor the mode row at one fixed offset in every mode including Analytics, and put real row actions with a visible link affordance on My work. Give 'See the records behind this' a disclosure affordance so it reads as expand-in-place rather than as navigation.

candidates.label: B
strengths: The best coverage-state vocabulary in the lab: hollow square for not-connected, filled amber square for partly-read, red target for failure — shape, colour and text together, repeated in the mode row and in the 'WHAT QUALIFIES THIS READ' rail, with failure additionally raising a full-width red 'FAILURE · PARTLY READ' band. Quiet, partial, failed and never-configured are four visibly different screens at both viewports.

The best briefing return in the lab. An explicit '‹ Back to Today' in the left margin, a 'TODAY / FULL BRIEFING' breadcrumb, and Today's nav underline changing from solid to dotted to say you are inside this mode one level down. That last detail is the most considered continuity gesture I saw anywhere in the set.

Disclosure affordances are unambiguous — 'See the records behind this ⌄' and '3 more things qualify this read ⌄' both read as expand-in-place — and the left gutter carries genuine marginalia ('2 asks in this thread.', '5 open, and at least one more that could not be counted.') rather than blank margin.
candidates.weakest: editorial__inbox__owner_signature__1440x960__fold.png — on an already-read item, 'Mark as read' renders as a live underlined link, and the refusal appears several lines below in body text as 'Mark as read: You have already read this.' A control that looks operable with a footnote saying it is not. Desk and Rail both solve this on the same row; this is the one place where a direction actively misleads the pointer.
concerns: The Inbox row action set is thin — Mark as read and Snooze only. No Clear from Inbox and no Approve at the source at the row, so journeys 7, 8 and 9 have no surface in the arrival state.
My work rows are links and nothing else; no direct action, so journey 11 has no expression.
The refusal-as-footnote pattern is the wrong shape and it is used consistently, so it is a systemic decision rather than one slip.
On owner_quiet the right two-fifths of the canvas is blank above the colophon; the coverage rail collapses to three lines and the remaining width is unmade.
The amber square beside each mode in the nav row carries no text of its own; the meaning only exists in the rail below, so the nav marker alone is colour-and-shape without a label.
candidates.requiredCorrection: Move the refusal onto the control. An action that cannot be taken must render as struck or otherwise plainly inoperable with its reason on the same line, never as a live link with a note underneath. Then add the missing dispositions to the Inbox row and at least one direct action to My work.

candidates.label: C
strengths: The leader-dot contents table is the single best idea in the lab for showing the state of a mode you are not in: four modes, a coverage verdict on each, and on provider_failure the whole table flips to 'Partly read · Not answering' with the glyph going from hollow to filled. It is legible in a quarter of a second.

Evidence disclosure is the most rigorous. COUNTED / LEFT OUT / CANNOT SAY / BASELINE as a definition list, with '2 of 23 records were left out of this' and 'No accepted baseline' stated before you expand 'See the records behind this +'. The documentary texture is earned rather than styled.

new_user is the most complete of the four: 'Nothing set up yet' on all four modes, a 'Where to start' block with a real primary button, and a 'WHAT LIMITED THIS READ / NOT CONNECTED — There is no project yet. Nothing failed, and nothing here counts as zero' block that explicitly refuses the failure reading.
candidates.weakest: index__today__owner_signature__1440x960.png — the full page shows the thesis failing. The contents table that IS the navigation sits at the top of a 2205px page, scrolls away, and the only recovery is a 'BACK TO THE TOP' link in the footer. Meanwhile the 550px right column holds about ten lines of text and is empty for roughly three-quarters of the page height, and it does not follow the scroll. The direction whose argument is that the index is the structure ships an index you cannot reach from inside the structure.
concerns: The mode navigation does not persist and has no substitute. Changing mode from the bottom of Today is scroll-to-top then click, on every mode, at every viewport.

The Inbox has no row actions at all — every event offers 'OPEN →' and nothing else, and My work is the same. Mark read, snooze, clear, approve and recover are all deferred to a detail surface that is not shown, so the arrival state is read-only. That is the direct opposite of direct actions on the row.

Scope change is a two-step. 'CHANGE WHAT HOME READS' is a 10px monospace underlined link in the right column; I could find no scope form control anywhere on the full page. The most frequently used global control in the product is the smallest, quietest thing on the screen.

Mobile is a compressed desktop, not a transformation. On index__today__provider_failure__390x844__fold.png the reader passes roughly 750px of contents table and accounting before reaching the headline — the entire first screen is chrome.
The right-hand column is the least-answered width in the lab: wide, mostly empty, static, and it carries the same two blocks in every mode.
candidates.requiredCorrection: The index must survive the scroll — condense it to a persistent bar, make it sticky, or otherwise keep the four modes reachable from any scroll position. Then put the dispositions back on the Inbox and My work rows so the arrival state can be acted on, and promote scope from a 10px link to a real labelled control in persistent chrome.

ballots.overallNote:
On my lens only A clears the 8.5 admission bar. That is a real finding, not a scoring accident, and I would rather say it than round three directions up to the gate.

The discriminator across the whole set is what a row does when an action is not available. Two directions (A, D) put the refusal on the control itself — struck through, with the reason on the same line — so nothing on screen lies about what it will do. One (B) renders the control as a live link and puts the refusal in body text below it. One (C) removes actions from the arrival state altogether and defers every disposition to a detail surface that is not in this evidence set. Since the captures contain no opened detail, C is effectively asking to be judged on a screen where nothing can be done, and that is the direction it chose.

Second discriminator: whether the navigation survives the scroll. A carries a stable four-band header plus an in-page section index; B and D carry compact chrome you can scroll back to quickly; C's contents table is both the entire navigation and the first 290px of a 2205px page, and its only recovery is a footer link. That is the most serious continuity defect in the lab, and it sits inside the direction whose whole thesis is the index.

Three things I could not judge and that no ballot should pretend to. Detail open and return is absent from all 160 captures — every shot is the arrival state with no ?item= or ?event= — so the axis these four directions were meant to differ on is untested. Motion is on its final frame everywhere, so each direction's signature gesture is unproven; the strongest implied one is D's failure band, which reads as a tear in the page. And dark theme was never rendered, which matters most for B and D, whose state vocabularies lean on amber and red.

One note for the programme rather than a candidate. The evidence README's descriptions of directions 2 and 4 are stale — D no longer has a 240px left sidebar, and A no longer renders new_user as a failed read. I judged the pixels. Anyone reading the prose summary instead of the images will score the wrong artefact.

candidates.label: A
strengths: The cap is proven to be judgement, not a limit. Today shows 'Today's signal 3' in the contents rail and '7 more qualified for today's signal and are not shown here'; the briefing shows the identical structure with 'Today's signal 10'. The reader sees the edit and the uncut version in the same grammar. No other candidate closes that loop.

One line of persistent chrome ('THE OTHER MODES · Partly read: Inbox and My work · Not enough history: Analytics') saves three speculative mode visits every morning, and it flips to 'Did not answer: Inbox, My work and Analytics' on failure. Highest value per pixel of any device in the lab.

Three distinct rule states under the headline — solid black (read), red (did not answer), dashed (nothing set up yet) — each paired with a lead word. A quiet day and a broken provider are distinguishable in peripheral vision, at 1440 and at 390.
candidates.weakest: desk__inbox__owner_signature__1440x960__fold.png — every event row carries its unavailable actions struck through with an explanation attached ('Approve at the source · This one is not an approval', 'Snooze · Only an open item can be snoozed'). Two dead controls and two justification clauses per row is honest at five events and a wall of crossed-out text at forty-two. This is the one surface where Desk competes with itself.
concerns: Today carries four sections — Today's signal 3, Needs review 3, Coming up 4, Moving well 2 — twelve rows and 2383px on the signature world. The cap is honoured on decisions, but the page below the cap is long, and 'Moving well' is a section whose defining property is that it needs no attention. It is real data, not invented furniture, but it is the closest thing in the lab to reassurance.

The three-tier header (products / modes + actor / coverage line) is roughly 120px of chrome above every page, the most of the four. The third tier earns it; the second tier repeating 'Orla. You own these projects' on every screen does not.

desk.css warms --paper with a color-mix, so Home alone sits on a different ground from the rest of the suite. Outside my lens, but it is a per-surface deviation from the vendored tokens and someone should decide it deliberately rather than inherit it from the wildcard licence.
Mobile stacks the coverage line under the mode row, pushing the headline to y≈267. Still the fastest of the four to a decision on a phone, but the margin is thinner than at desktop.
candidates.requiredCorrection: Cut the disabled-action noise in Inbox. Keep the refusal reasons, but move them behind the row (on the disabled control, on demand) rather than rendering two struck-through labels plus two explanatory clauses on every event. At scale this surface is where Desk's attention discipline breaks down.

candidates.label: B
strengths: 01 / 02 / 03 in a monospaced margin is the clearest statement in the lab that these three are ranked. It reads as an editor's running order rather than the top of a truncated list — precisely the difference between judgement and an arbitrary cut.

The most disciplined state system of the four: filled amber square (coverage limited), red concentric target (failure), hollow square (nothing connected). Different shapes, not different colours, and the marker disappears entirely when a mode is fine — at scale, Analytics loses its marker because history is now sufficient. The marker therefore means something.
The quiet day is the sparest screen in the lab: headline, one honest sentence naming why it is still not an all clear, one link, then the colophon. Nothing is invented to fill the space.
candidates.weakest: editorial__inbox__owner_signature__1440x960__fold.png — the thread rows sit in a nested indented box that stops roughly 560px short of the right edge, leaving the largest unexplained dead zone in the lab, and 'Mark as read: You have already read this.' floats as a sentence with no control attached to it. The composition stops being a list and the width stops being a decision.
concerns: At 1440 the row title ends around x=768 and its lateness sits at x=1180. The single most decision-relevant datum on the row is a 400px saccade from the thing it describes, on every row, every day. That is a small tax paid many times.

The amber square appears four times across the top nav on the signature world. Individually quiet, collectively it is the closest thing in the lab to a chip row, and in the nav it carries meaning without a text label (the label lives only in the right panel).

Inbox row actions are limited to Mark as read and Snooze on arrival; disposition and clearing are deferred to the opened event. Daily triage is therefore slower than Desk's, and the README confirms the detail state is not in evidence, so I cannot verify the recovery there.

The 'HOW THIS PAGE WAS READ' colophon is a good answer to the width question at the foot, but the page above it still leaves the right third empty on Today and Inbox. The answer is applied to one region and not to the page.
candidates.requiredCorrection: Bind lateness to its row. Bring the date and lateness inboard so the eye does not cross 400px of white to learn whether a decision is four days late, and give Inbox's thread block a reason to use the width it occupies — provenance, read-state, or the correspondence it currently withholds.

candidates.label: C
strengths: The leader-dot contents table is the best cross-mode orientation idea in the lab. '01 Today ……… Read · Not connected / 02 Inbox ……… Partly read' reports the coverage of every mode from inside any mode, as a table rather than a marker. On provider failure all four rows flip to 'Partly read · Not answering' and the honesty is total.

The Analytics receipt structure — COUNTED / LEFT OUT / CANNOT SAY / BASELINE as a fielded definition list under each number — is the most rigorous evidence presentation of the four. '2 of 23 records were left out of this' is exactly the sentence the governing rule exists to force.

The full-width tinted 'WHAT LIMITED THIS READ' block spans both columns and is unmissable. New user gets its own variant ('NOT CONNECTED · There is no project yet. Nothing failed, and nothing here counts as zero') with a real indigo Open Tasks button.
candidates.weakest: index__today__provider_failure__390x844__fold.png — the contents table, then the WHAT HOME READ panel, then the red limitation block, and only at y≈738 the headline, with the standfirst cut off at the fold. On a phone, on the worst morning of the month, the first screen contains no decision at all — only three stacked layers of the page describing itself.
concerns: The contents table costs about 290px above the headline on every arrival, in every mode, forever. On day one it is orientation; on day two hundred the reader knows the four modes and the only live information is four status words on the right — which Desk and Rail deliver in a single line at a tenth of the cost. It front-loads navigation ahead of the decision the page exists to deliver.

The right column (WHAT HOME READ / THIS READ) is structurally identical on every mode and every scenario. Roughly 450px of the 1440 is a fixed metadata panel that never varies, which is how a reader learns to stop looking at a region of the screen.

The quiet day still renders the full contents table and both right panels above a single-sentence answer. Nothing was invented to look busy, but nothing stepped back either — this is the worst chrome-to-content ratio in the lab on the day that most needs restraint.
Inbox rows offer only 'OPEN →'. No mark-as-read, no snooze, no clear on the row. Every disposition costs a navigation, which is the slowest daily triage of the four.

At 390 the right-aligned status text runs flush to the viewport edge — 'Not answering' terminates at x≈373 of 390. Longer strings will clip or overflow, and the baseline floor is no horizontal scroll at 320px.
candidates.requiredCorrection: The contents table must earn its toll or shrink. Either collapse it to a single line after first arrival (keeping the four status words, dropping the numbered leader-dot rows), or move it below the headline so the decision leads and the index follows. On mobile it must not be possible for the first screen to contain zero decisions — least of all on provider failure.

candidates.label: D
strengths: The mode row with a text coverage label under every mode name is the most direct answer in the lab to 'what is happening in the modes I am not in'. READ / PARTLY READ / NOT ENOUGH HISTORY, and on failure four red DID NOT ANSWER stamps plus the scope control itself flipping to DID NOT ANSWER. No marker to decode, no table to read.

The striped band on provider failure — red rules top and bottom with interrupted grey stripes around the sentence — is the most legible and most memorable failure treatment of the four, and it survives 390 intact. A broken provider and a quiet day are not merely different here, they are different objects.

'THE EDGE OF THIS READ · Looking fourteen days ahead · Nothing below this line is asking for you inside this read.' names the horizon of the read instead of implying completeness. It is the one signature moment in the lab that does real work on the governing rule rather than decorating it.
candidates.weakest: rail__inbox__owner_signature__1440x960__fold.png — the right column permanently displays 'WHEN A SNOOZE COMES BACK · LATER TODAY: 18:00 on Thursday 16 July · PICK A TIME: 01:30 on Sunday 25 October · PICK A TIME: 02:00 on Sunday 28 March.' Those are daylight-saving edge cases, rendered on arrival, before anything has been snoozed, in the most peripherally prominent column on the page. A test fixture has leaked onto the reading surface and it competes for attention with zero user value on an ordinary morning.
concerns: Today's three decisions are not numbered. Every other direction ranks them 01/02/03; D relies on order and a lateness gutter. 'At most three ranked decisions' is the product's central claim, and D is the only candidate where three items can be read as the first three of a longer list rather than an editor's top three. This is the direct hit on my lens.

Inbox row actions are set in indigo — Mark as read, Snooze, Clear from Inbox, three to four per row. Indigo is the anchor colour; spending it on repeated row verbs across forty-two events makes Inbox the loudest surface in the lab and drains the anchor of meaning.
'Nothing stands between now and the edge of this read' is the most oblique sentence in the set. The horizon idea is good; the phrasing is figurative where the one unbendable rule is plain English.
The mode row sits below the standfirst on Analytics and above it on Today, Inbox and My work. The row is the primary orientation device and it should not move.

New user leads straight from the mode row into 'Where to start' with no sentence naming what happened; the honest line ('There is no project yet. Nothing failed, and nothing here counts as zero') is only in the right column. The action is prominent, the explanation is peripheral — the wrong way round on somebody's first screen.
candidates.requiredCorrection: Two things. Remove the snooze-schedule panel from the Inbox arrival state — surface it when a snooze is actually being set, never before. And rank Today's three decisions visibly, so the cap reads as an editor's order rather than the top of a list.

ballots.overallNote:
Judged only on daily workflow and attention integrity. No vetoes: all four honour the fixed architecture, and not one of them renders missing, stale, failed or unconfigured data as zero, empty or all clear. On that governing rule the lab has genuinely succeeded — every candidate makes a quiet day and a broken provider different objects, at both viewports, and every candidate gives a new reader a plain sentence and a real Open Tasks button rather than an error.

The separation is in what each direction charges the reader for that honesty. The test I applied is a boring one: on an ordinary Thursday at 08:40, how much of the first screen is the page describing itself, and how much is the decision I came for.

A is the clear leader because it is the only direction that proves the cap. Today says 'Today's signal 3' and 'seven more qualified and are not shown here'; the briefing says 'Today's signal 10' in the identical structure. The reader can see the edit against the uncut version, which is the difference between editorial judgement and an arbitrary number. Its failure line — 'Some sources did not answer, so this list can be short. Short is not empty.' — is the single best sentence in the lab, because it defuses the exact misreading the cap invites. Its cost is a twelve-row Today and a noisy Inbox, both correctable.

B is close and is the most disciplined system: three state markers by shape not colour, the marker vanishing when a mode is genuinely fine, and 01/02/03 making the ranking explicit. It loses ground on ergonomics rather than principle — a 400px eye-journey from each title to its lateness, and an Inbox that abandons a third of the canvas.

D has the best orientation device (every mode's read state in words, in the mode row) and the best failure treatment, and it forfeits some of that by not ranking its three decisions and by parking daylight-saving edge cases in the Inbox's right column on arrival. Both are small fixes; together they are the difference between 8.2 and a pass.

C is the most rigorous on evidence and has the best single idea in the lab — the leader-dot contents table that reports every mode's coverage from inside any mode. It is ranked last because it charges for that idea on every arrival forever. On a phone, on provider failure, the first screen contains three stacked layers of metadata and no decision. A direction whose job is to answer 'what deserves attention now' must not put its own structure first on the worst morning of the month.

One caveat on the evidence itself: no capture shows a selected row, no capture shows motion, and no capture shows dark theme. Detail behaviour is one of the axes these four are meant to differ on and none of it is visible, so my Inbox judgements are about the arrival state only. A's and D's row-action noise, and B's and C's row-action absence, could all read differently once an event is open. That does not change the ranking, but it does mean the Inbox scores are the least certain numbers on this ballot.

candidates.label: A
strengths: The only direction that publishes a written key for its own marks. The foot legend states in plain words that every mark repeats something the row already says, then lists all five shapes with their meanings (filled square / open square / open circle / filled dot / break). Nothing on the page needs colour to be understood, and the page says so.

Quiet, failure and new-user are separated on four redundant channels at once: the rule under the headline changes treatment (solid black / red / dashed), the lead phrase changes ("Read." / "Did not answer." / "Nothing set up yet."), an extra section appears at the foot on failure ("What this read could not see"), and the spine breaks with its own glyph. A greyscale reader and a colour-blind reader both get it at a glance.

Per-mode coverage is a sentence, not a badge: "THE OTHER MODES · Partly read: Inbox and My work | Not enough history: Analytics" sits under the mode row at full text contrast, on every screen, at both viewports.
candidates.weakest: desk__inbox__owner_signature__1440x960__fold.png
concerns: Link affordance is the weakest of the four. Row actions ("Mark as read", "Snooze", "Clear from Inbox") carry no underline and no colour, so an operable control is visually identical to body prose. Nothing on the arrival screen tells a reader what can be clicked.

Unavailable actions are struck through in the same dark ink ("Approve at the source" with "This one is not an approval." beside it). Strikethrough hurts legibility and is a weak disabled signal; if those elements remain focusable, a keyboard user tabs through dead controls to reach live ones.

Target size. The action cluster is a row of ~17px text links packed horizontally with small gaps, and at 390 the four mode labels sit on one ~20px line. Nothing approaches 44x44 for primary controls on a coarse pointer.

The "IN THIS READ" contents rail sits outside the white content panel, in the page margin, at low contrast. Its relationship to main is visually ambiguous at 1440 and it disappears entirely at 390, so the two viewports offer different orientation.
Overdue text is red at ~13px on warm paper. The words carry the meaning so it is not colour-alone, but the red is doing real work at a size where it is doing it least well.
candidates.requiredCorrection: Give operable text actions a visible affordance (underline or indigo, matching the direction's own link style), and replace strikethrough-disabled with a non-focusable, properly contrasted unavailable state. Raise action hit areas to 44px on coarse pointers.

candidates.label: B
strengths: The status band is the fastest at-a-glance read in the lab and its primary carrier is text: a full-width rule with a small-caps label set beside it ("FAILURE · PARTLY READ", "COVERAGE · PARTLY READ", "NOT CONNECTED · NOTHING SET UP YET"). State is named, not implied.
Every row title is an underlined link, consistently, across all four modes. Of the four directions this is the only one where a reader can tell what is operable without hovering.
The colophon gives every page one findable, consistently placed home for provenance, accounting and limits, so "where do I look for what this page could not see" has the same answer in every mode.
candidates.weakest: editorial__analytics__owner_signature__1440x960__fold.png
concerns: The amber marker in the mode row is the only in-nav signal that Inbox, My work and Analytics are limited, and it fails non-text contrast. Measured against white it is roughly 2:1, well under the 3:1 floor for a graphic that carries meaning. The same amber draws the full-width status rule on Inbox and My work, so on those pages the highest-level state banner is the lowest-contrast element on the screen.

One glyph, two meanings. The identical amber square marks "Partly read" and "Not enough history"; the distinction exists only in the side panel. A reader scanning the nav learns that something is limited but not what, and the marker carries no inline text.

Analytics separates a claim from its number by roughly 800px: "Items that are not in a Done column right now." begins at the left of the measure and "19 OPEN WORK" is set hard against the right edge. At 200% and 400% zoom the two fall out of the same view and the association is lost.

The Analytics label/value pairs look mis-assigned ("WHAT THE RECORDS SAY" paired with "No accepted baseline"; no "LEFT OUT" label at all). A description list read aloud verbatim will state the wrong relationship.
Row rules run the full 1440 while the text sits in the middle measure, so the visible rule is not the boundary of anything a pointer can hit and the row's clickable extent is unguessable.
candidates.requiredCorrection: Raise the amber marker and the amber status rule to at least 3:1 against paper, and give the mode-row marker an inline text state (or distinct glyphs per state) so "partly read" and "not enough history" are separable in the nav. Move the Analytics figure adjacent to its claim and correct the label/value pairing.

candidates.label: C
strengths: The leader-dot contents table is the best navigation idea in the lab on my lens. Every mode's coverage is stated in words, in the nav, readable from any other mode ("01 Today ....... Read · Not connected", "04 Analytics ....... Not enough history"). None of it depends on colour, and at 390 the rows are the largest mode targets of the four directions.

Fielded, labelled metadata throughout: Inbox rows read "READ · Not read yet | STATE · Still open", and Analytics uses COUNTED / LEFT OUT / CANNOT SAY / BASELINE. This is the most screen-reader-legible information structure of the four, and it puts each number directly under the claim it belongs to.
The failure state announces itself with a text heading, not just a tint: "WHAT LIMITED THIS READ / NOT ANSWERING" above the headline, with the same block reused for new-user as "NOT CONNECTED".
candidates.weakest: index__today__new_user__1440x960.png
concerns: The primary action on a new person's first ever screen fails contrast. "Open Tasks" is near-black text on indigo #4f46e5, roughly 3:1, short of the 4.5:1 required for a button label. This is the one control Amendment 2 says must exist, and candidate D ships the identical button with white text and passes, so this is a defect rather than a taste difference.

Provenance is set in a light warm monospace ("Tasks · Nora & Cian") measuring around 3:1 at ~12px. Provenance is required to be quiet but always visible; at this contrast it is quiet but not reliably visible.

Inbox events expose one small "OPEN →" link, roughly 46x14px, as the only per-row target. Every disposition is deferred to a detail view that is not in evidence, so on a phone the whole mode is a stack of sub-44px text links.
At 390 the contents-table status wraps onto its own right-aligned second line, splitting each mode's name from its state and putting the two on different lines and different alignments.
The pink failure band spans the full page width and runs under the right column, displacing the "THIS READ" panel. The failure notice and the read panel collide in the same horizontal band.
candidates.requiredCorrection: Set the "Open Tasks" button label to white on indigo (4.5:1 or better) before anything else; this blocks the first-run screen. Raise the monospace provenance to at least 4.5:1, and give Inbox rows a real disposition target of 44px rather than a single small "OPEN" link.

candidates.label: D
strengths: The state of all four modes is written under all four mode labels, on every screen, in every scenario: READ / PARTLY READ / NOT ENOUGH HISTORY / NOTHING IN IT / DID NOT ANSWER / NOTHING SET UP YET. No other direction keeps every mode's coverage in words that permanently visible, and it makes the quiet-versus-broken distinction unmissable before you read a single row.

The clearest available-versus-unavailable action language in the lab. Live actions are indigo links at comfortable contrast ("Mark as read", "Snooze", "Clear from Inbox"); unavailable ones are grey and struck with a written reason immediately beside them ("Approve at the source · This one is not an approval."). Colour, weight, decoration and prose all agree.

The only new-user screen whose primary action meets contrast: "Open Tasks" set white on indigo. The failure band (red rules with hairline ruling around the sentence) is also genuinely distinct and captioned in words rather than left to the colour.
candidates.weakest: rail__today__owner_signature__390x844.png
concerns: Two link styles on one page, one of them invisible. Row titles such as "Wait for the Ballyhoura venue confirmation" carry no underline and no colour, while "Open the full briefing" in the same view is indigo and underlined. A reader cannot infer which text is operable.

The load-bearing per-mode status captions are ~10px monospace in a mid-grey measuring around 3.5:1, under the 4.5:1 floor for small text, and their severity bar is amber at roughly 2:1. The direction's single best accessibility idea is executed at its worst contrast.

Reading order at 390 is the weakest of the four. The right-column material (THE READ / WHAT WAS READ / NOTHING PRODUCES THIS YET) is dropped into the middle of the document, between "Coming up" and "Moving well", so page metadata interrupts the section sequence rather than following it.
At 390 the mode row wraps so Analytics and its status land on a second line, breaking the four modes into an uneven two-line group with mismatched alignment.

The Home mode navigation sits after the h1 rather than before it, so the four modes are not the first thing reached after the products nav. Defensible as composition, but it costs orientation for keyboard and screen-reader users arriving at the page.
candidates.requiredCorrection: Raise the per-mode status captions to at least 4.5:1 and their severity bars to 3:1, and give row titles the same visible link treatment the direction already uses for "Open the full briefing". Move the right-column read metadata to the end of the document at 390 so section order is not interrupted.

ballots.overallNote:
On the governing rule all four pass, and that is the genuine achievement of this lab: in every direction a quiet day, a failed provider and a new account are separable at a glance, and in every direction the separation is carried by words rather than by hue alone. I could not fault any of them on that. So the ranking is decided by the ordinary craft underneath it, and there the four are not close.

A is the only one I can admit on my lens. It is the only direction that publishes a key to its own visual language and states, in the interface, that the marks repeat what the words already say. It stacks four redundant channels on the state distinction (rule treatment, lead phrase, an extra section on failure, a broken spine glyph), and its state text is set at full contrast in ordinary ink rather than in a tint that has to be squinted at. Its flaw is real and broad: no row action anywhere is visually distinguishable from prose, and unavailable actions are struck through rather than properly de-emphasised. That is one CSS rule and one state style, and it does not touch the structure.

D is the most explicit direction and I nearly ranked it first. Every mode's coverage is written under every mode label on every screen, and it has the clearest available/unavailable action language and the only new-user button that meets contrast. It loses the top slot because the idea I most want to praise is executed at ~3.5:1 in 10px monospace with a 2:1 severity bar, and because its 390 reading order drops page metadata into the middle of the section sequence.

B has the best link affordance and the best typography, and its status band is the fastest read in the lab. But its in-nav state marker fails non-text contrast at roughly 2:1, uses one glyph for two different meanings, and on Inbox and My work the page's top-level status rule is the lowest-contrast element on the screen. Its Analytics separates a claim from its number by 800px and mislabels the pairs.

C has the strongest structural ideas of any direction — the contents table and the fielded COUNTED / LEFT OUT / CANNOT SAY / BASELINE list are the most legible information architecture here, and its mode nav has the largest mobile targets. It ranks last only because the execution repeatedly undercuts the thinking: near-black on indigo for the one action on a new person's first screen, ~3:1 provenance, and a single 46x14px link as the entire disposition surface of a mode. None of that is a reason to reject the direction; all of it is a reason it cannot be admitted as it stands.

No vetoes. One Pass, three Revise. I want to record one limit on this ballot honestly: no capture shows focus, no capture shows a selected row or an opened detail, no capture shows dark theme or forced colours, and no capture shows keyboard order. Focus visibility, focus return on detail open and close, and forced-colours survival are three of the largest risks on my lens and none of them is in evidence. My scores are therefore a ceiling, not a clearance, and whichever direction is picked should be re-examined on those three before the 9.5 gate.

candidates.label: D
strengths: Puts the h1 above the mode navigation, so at 390 a phone reader knows what is being asked at y≈175 and never reads a wall of navigation before content. Structurally the best answer in the lab to the question my lens exists to ask.

Row structure genuinely re-composes rather than squeezing: the right-aligned margin stamp ("4 days late", "As read on Thursday 16 July") becomes a small-caps lead-in line above the title at 390. Same information, different composition.

The right column carries different material per mode (accounting on Today, "WHEN A SNOOZE COMES BACK" on Inbox, the history window on Analytics), and at 390 it linearises into a named colophon with "THE EDGE OF THIS READ / Nothing below this line is asking for you inside this read" explaining the reordering. The width is answered and so is the stack.
candidates.weakest: rail__today__owner_signature__390x844__fold.png — the mode row wraps to two rows because "NOT ENOUGH HISTORY" is wide, pushing the first decision to y≈707 of 844 (84%); the identical page at scale fits one row and shows two decisions, so the arrival screen is hostage to a label length.
concerns: Mode-row wrapping at 390 is state-dependent: one row at scale, 2+2 at provider_failure, 3+1 at inbox and analytics. The arrival composition changes shape with the data, and in the worst case costs ~130px of the first screen.

Today at 390 is the tallest mobile page in the set (3758px). Two desktop columns become one long stack with no viewport-specific collapse anywhere, so the phone pays in full for everything the desktop shows side by side.

The shell's vertical order differs by mode: on Analytics the standfirst sits above the mode row, on Today it sits below the content rule. At 390 that moves the navigation up and down the page between modes, which reads unsettled.

At 1440 the Inbox left gutter (~185px) carries only a timestamp and the amber coverage rule stops at x≈800 while the content column runs to x≈965. Ragged edges on the mode where width pressure is highest.

The failure block (broken hairlines between two red rules) is the strongest signature in the lab and survives 390 intact, but it is the only place the full width does expressive work; on quiet and new_user the middle-left of the 1440 canvas is simply blank.

candidates.label: A
strengths: Best content-per-phone-screen in the set. At 390 the header is a compact ~205px carrying all four text-labelled modes on one line, the scope control and the per-mode coverage line, and the first decision title lands at y≈550 of 844 with two decision titles visible on the signature world.

Rows genuinely reflow: "Needs review" is title-left / provenance-right at 1440 and stacks to title-then-meta at 390. The "IN THIS READ" contents rail is dropped on the phone rather than stacked, and its counts survive inside the section headings, so nothing is lost and no wall is created.

Unknown stays unknown through a non-colour device that survives the transform: solid black rule for a complete read, red rule for a failed one, dashed rule for nothing-set-up-yet. All three are legible at 390, and new_user's "Open Tasks" is fully above the fold at y≈578.
candidates.weakest: desk__inbox__owner_signature__1440x960__fold.png — the contents rail that justifies the left 264px on Today and Analytics simply vanishes on Inbox, leaving both the left 264px and the right 264px of a 1440 screen as unexplained warm ground on the mode with the most material.
concerns: The collapse of "Coming up" and "Moving well" behind chevrons is identical at 1440 and 390, so it is a shared device, not a mobile transformation. Strip the dropped rail and the phone page is the desktop page with one column removed — done well, but inherited rather than re-composed.
The spine (vertical rule plus indigo squares) is retained at 390, costing roughly 30px of a 390 viewport to a device that is doing almost no work at that width.

Inbox row actions at 390 ("Mark as read  Snooze" / "Approve at the source…" / "Clear from Inbox") are small inline text links wrapping to three tightly stacked lines. These look well under the 44×44 coarse-pointer floor the brief sets for primary controls.
The mobile header stacks four bands (products, scope, modes, coverage) — complete and text-labelled, which is right, but roughly 24% of the phone screen before the dateline.
Warm paper is a real identity, but it is the only direction whose canvas differs from the design system's default, which is a token-level commitment, not a per-lab one.

candidates.label: B
strengths: The most craftful reflow in the lab. The right-aligned field labels of Analytics (COUNTED / CANNOT SAY / WINDOW) become inline lead-ins at 390 ("COUNTED 19 open items…"), and Inbox's margin note "2 asks in this thread" moves under the thread title. A two-dimensional structure becomes a one-dimensional one on purpose.

At 1440 the three zones are genuinely different material — dateline and field labels left, measure centre, coverage rail and lateness right. Analytics is the best-composed wide page in the set and answers Amendment 1 without inventing furniture.

The provider failure treatment reuses the otherwise-empty left margin as the label zone: a full-bleed double red rule with "FAILURE · PARTLY READ" set in it, and the whole device survives the transform to 390 unchanged and unmissable.
candidates.weakest: editorial__today__new_user__390x844__fold.png — a person's first ever screen on a phone puts the one action, "Open Tasks", at y≈818 of 844, clipped by the fold behind a masthead, a product row, a mode row, a scope row, a dateline, a standfirst and a coverage legend.
concerns: The right coverage rail linearises straight into the primary reading flow ahead of the content at 390, so the first decision title falls at y≈635 (75%) on the signature world and its body is at the screen edge. Meta before matter is the wrong order on a phone.

The rail's collapse ("3 more things qualify this read ⌄") is content-driven, not viewport-driven — the same collapse fires at 1440 and the same four-line list renders at 390. No viewport-specific disclosure anywhere in the direction.

At 1440 Inbox leaves the region below the coverage rail and right of the thread rows blank for roughly 350px of column across the full height of the queue. The mode where width is hardest to spend is the one where it is spent least.

Mode state is announced by a small amber square in the navigation; the text that explains it lives in the rail. At 390 both are present, but the marker and its legend are separated by the standfirst, which weakens the pairing on the viewport where it matters most.
8.2 on my lens is below the 8.5 admission bar. This is a small correction, not a redesign, but it is not admissible as rendered.
candidates.requiredCorrection: At 390, move "WHAT QUALIFIES THIS READ" below the first decision (or collapse it to a single summary line with a disclosure at narrow widths only), and guarantee that on new_user the "Open Tasks" control clears the 844 fold. The desktop three-zone composition should not change.

candidates.label: C
strengths: The leader-dot contents table that doubles as mode navigation and as a per-mode coverage report is the single best wide-screen idea in the lab: at 1440 the state of a mode you are not in is legible from the mode you are in, and at provider_failure all four rows flip to "Partly read · Not answering" at once.

The "WHAT LIMITED THIS READ" band spans both columns with a red top rule and a red left bar, and it is the fastest failure read at 1440. new_user degrades to the same block without the tint, so not-yet and broken are visibly different.
Analytics at 1440 sets each claim as a labelled record (COUNTED / LEFT OUT / CANNOT SAY / BASELINE) — a documentary texture that suits the governing rule better than any chart would.
candidates.weakest: index__today__new_user__390x844__fold.png — a new person's entire first phone screen is a four-row contents index saying "Nothing set up yet" four times plus a metadata block. The h1 is at the bottom edge, the "Where to start" action is entirely below the fold, and there is no content of any kind on screen.
concerns: This is the squeezed desktop my lens is built to catch. Nothing collapses, nothing re-composes, and Today at 390 is 3122px of stacked 1440 layout. The contents index survives verbatim as a ~250px wall of navigation ahead of the headline in every scenario.

The leader dots are retained at 390 but the status has wrapped to the following line, so the dots now lead to nothing. The device that carries the whole direction is broken by the reflow rather than adapted to it.

At 390 the status labels ("Not connected", "Not enough history", "Read") sit flush against the right edge with no gutter while body text has ~16px, and the active-mode indigo underline runs full-bleed while the hairlines above it stop short. At 390 the right margin is already zero, which puts the stated 320px no-horizontal-overflow floor at real risk.

On the signature world the first decision title lands at y≈790 of 844 with its body clipped; at provider_failure no decision is on the phone's first screen at all. The most important thing on the page is behind the navigation in every scenario I opened.

At 1440 the right rail repeats largely the same "WHAT HOME READ" block on every mode and then stops, leaving roughly 500px of empty column below it on Inbox and Analytics — a second column that is present rather than earned.
candidates.requiredCorrection: At narrow widths the contents index must stop being a wall: collapse it to the current mode plus a labelled disclosure (all four modes must remain text-labelled and reachable, never behind More or an icon), place it after the h1, and move the "WHAT HOME READ" block below the first decision. Give the status column a real right gutter and stop the active underline at the same edge as the hairlines, then re-test at 390 and 320. Until the first decision and the new_user action clear the fold, this direction cannot be admitted.

ballots.overallNote: Judged only on responsive and mobile composition, 390 against 1440, this lab splits cleanly in two. D and A treat the phone as a place with its own order of business: D puts the headline above the navigation so nothing important ever sits behind a nav wall, and re-composes row structure (margin stamps become small-caps lead-ins, the accounting rail becomes a colophon with a named edge line); A gets the most decisions onto the first phone screen and drops its contents rail cleanly while preserving its counts in the section headings. B is the finest typographic craft in the set and its label-to-lead-in reflow is the best single piece of responsive work here, but it stacks its coverage rail ahead of the content, so meta precedes matter on every phone screen and a new person's one action is clipped by the fold. C has the most intelligent 1440 in the lab and the least designed 390: the contents index survives verbatim as a wall of navigation, its leader dots lead nowhere once the status wraps, its status column sits flush against the viewport edge with no gutter, and on new_user and provider_failure there is no content on the phone's first screen at all. Two findings cut across all four and belong to the programme rather than to any team. First, none of the four uses a single viewport-specific disclosure — every collapse I found (Desk's chevrons, Editorial's \"3 more things qualify this read\") fires identically at 1440 and 390, so every direction pays the full desktop page height on a phone. Second, the phone header is where the four differ most and where the brief's own floor bites hardest: A and D keep all four modes text-labelled and above the fold at every scenario I opened, B and C push real content off the first screen to do it. On the governing rule, mobile is where it is won or lost, and it holds up best in D (the torn-line failure block reads instantly at 390) and A (solid, red and dashed rules distinguish read, failed and not-yet without relying on colour); C's failure band survives the transform but arrives on a screen with nothing else on it. Only A and D clear my 8.5 bar as rendered.
